1	# Dock Lightning-Fast Architecture Fix Plan - 2026-06-04
2	
3	## Status
4	
5	Version: `v0`
6	
7	This is a living architecture plan. It is intentionally not an implementation
8	patch. The first version captures the current evidence and the target shape so
9	the model-consensus pass can critique and simplify it.
10	
11	Required external review gates:
12	
13	- `$model-consensus` with `opus 4.8 max` and `gpt 5.5 xhigh`.
14	- `$fresh-consult` with Cursor Agent `composer-2.5-fast`.
15	- Do not implement in this pass.
16	
17	## Source Evidence
18	
19	Primary diagnostic input:
20	
21	- `docs/IPHONE_17_PRO_DOCK_LAG_PROFILE_WORKLOG_2026-06-04.md`
22	
23	Key measured facts:
24	
25	- At `1,247` loaded Dock rows, `DockView.dockScreenValue` builds a `469,211`
26	  character accessibility payload in `20-22 ms`, repeatedly.
27	- The same runtime window logs frame hitches up to `103 ms`.
28	- `home` alone reproduces the hitch pattern at `978` rows; `M5` alone is much
29	  smoother at `269` rows.
30	- The data/projection pipeline is measurable but not the dominant visible cost:
31	  steady-state `dock.render.project` averaged `8 ms`,
32	  `dock.data_engine.snapshot` averaged `9 ms`, and `dock.main_publish` averaged
33	  `1 ms` in the final simulator proof.
34	- Untouched idle app runtime still rebuilt the full Dock root payload on host
35	  heartbeat/update publishes.
36	
37	Relevant owner paths:
38	
39	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`
40	- `CodexDock/Dock/DockScreenStore.swift`
41	- `CodexDock/Dock/DockRenderProjector.swift`
42	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`
43	- `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`
44	- `CodexDockUITests/DisplayedUICaptureSupport.swift`
45	- `README.md`
46	
47	## Problem Statement
48	
49	The Dock has crossed a boundary where normal screen updates can no longer carry
50	test/proof payloads or all-row derived state through SwiftUI body evaluation.
51	The current architecture lets a single host heartbeat trigger a full combined
52	Dock publish. That publish invalidates SwiftUI, and the Dock header computes a
53	root accessibility value that includes every rendered row's automation value.
54	
55	The visible symptom is scroll lag, but the architecture problem is broader:
56	high-frequency data events are allowed to force large main-thread UI work that
57	is proportional to total row count.
58	
59	## Target Architecture
60	
61	The target is a Dock screen contract where user interaction cost is bounded by
62	visible UI, not by total Dock dataset size.
63	
64	Performance guarantees:
65	
66	- Main-thread work on heartbeat/no-visible-change events is `O(1)` or skipped.
67	- Main-thread work on a visible row update is proportional to the changed visible
68	  rows, not all rows.
69	- Scroll-time work is bounded by the viewport and nearby lazy rows.
70	- Test/proof extraction never runs as a normal SwiftUI accessibility value.
71	- Automation state is still deterministic, structured, and strict enough to
72	  catch UI drift.
73	- The architecture has one owner for publish eligibility and one owner for
74	  automation snapshots, so future code cannot reintroduce bulk payloads in view
75	  bodies.
76	
77	## Proposed Shape For Model Critique
78	
79	Create a central `DockRenderPipeline` concept owned by the Dock screen layer.
80	It should replace ad hoc "publish every combined snapshot" behavior with a
81	single place that decides whether a new host event changes the rendered Dock
82	screen.
83	
84	The pipeline has three products:
85	
86	1. `DockScreenModel`: small, Equatable, main-actor state for SwiftUI.
87	2. `DockRenderDataset`: off-main full-row data used by projection, search,
88	   filters, grouping, and details.
89	3. `DockAutomationSnapshot`: structured, on-demand proof data for UI tests and
90	   sync scripts.
91	
92	The important rule: `DockView` can render `DockScreenModel`, but it must not
93	derive all-row automation payloads from body evaluation.
94	
95	## Central Patterns To Introduce
96	
97	### 1. Publish Gate
98	
99	Add a single publish gate before `DockScreenStore` emits `.loaded`.
100	
101	Inputs:
102	
103	- Current rendered screen fingerprint.
104	- Next host snapshot metadata.
105	- Next combined projection fingerprint.
106	- Pending local UI overlays such as optimistic renames.
107	- Current projection options: lens, search, filters, collapsed groups.
108	
109	Outputs:
110	
111	- `skip`: no visible or automation-relevant screen change.
112	- `metadataOnly`: update connectivity/status side channels without invalidating
113	  the Dock row tree.
114	- `publish`: emit a new `DockScreenModel`.
115	
116	The gate should reject heartbeat-only publishes when the ordered visible row IDs
117	and row display fingerprints are unchanged.
118	
119	### 2. Stable Row Display Fingerprints
120	
121	Each `DockRowViewModel` needs a compact fingerprint that represents only fields
122	that can change rendered row UI or row automation truth:
123	
124	- identity: host, source host, projection ID, thread ID
125	- display ordering key
126	- status/origin/relationship
127	- repository, branch, label presence, color rail
128	- summary/title/last activity text used on the row
129	- pin state and pinned ordering fields
130	
131	The fingerprint is the comparison primitive. The UI should not diff whole
132	payload strings.
133	
134	### 3. Viewport-Bounded SwiftUI Contract
135	
136	Keep `LazyVStack`, but make the state SwiftUI observes smaller:
137	
138	- `DockScreenModel` contains summary/header/filter state, visible row section
139	  identities, and row view models needed for the current projection.
140	- Rows remain individually identified by stable row identity.
141	- Expensive all-row proof data and full encoded `rowValues` do not live in
142	  `DockView`.
143	
144	The plan should decide whether `DockScreenModel` still carries all projected
145	rows for `LazyVStack` or whether it introduces an indexed collection/view model
146	that supports viewport-window extraction. The default preference is minimal:
147	first remove bulk accessibility work and no-op publishes, then add true windowing
148	only if profiling still shows total-row render cost.
149	
150	### 4. Automation Snapshot Service
151	
152	Replace Dock root `rowValues=` with a centralized test/proof path.
153	
154	Candidate shape:
155	
156	- `DockAutomationSnapshotStore` owned next to `DockScreenStore`.
157	- It receives accepted `DockRenderSnapshot` values off the main interaction path.
158	- It exposes compact screen state on the root accessibility value:
159	  `loaded; rows=1247; visibleRows=1247; revision=26; automationSnapshot=26`.
160	- UI tests and simulator proof scripts fetch full row proof data through a
161	  dedicated, explicitly test-only route.
162	
163	The route could be:
164	
165	- A hidden accessibility element with paged/chunked row payloads created only
166	  when `CODEX_DOCK_UI_TESTING=1`.
167	- A simulator-only app-container JSON snapshot written by the app when
168	  `CODEX_DOCK_UI_TESTING=1`.
169	- A local app diagnostic endpoint only in UI-test launch mode.
170	
171	The model-consensus pass must choose the smallest robust route and specify how
172	scripts/tests migrate.
173	
174	### 5. Performance Budget Tests
175	
176	Add tests that fail when regressions reappear:
177	
178	- Unit test the publish gate: heartbeat/no-row-change does not publish.
179	- Unit test row fingerprints: display-relevant changes publish; invisible
180	  metadata-only changes do not.
181	- Unit test root accessibility value length stays bounded at high row count.
182	- UI performance proof: with 1,200+ rows and both hosts, no all-row
183	  accessibility rebuilds occur during idle/scroll.
184	- Contract proof migration: displayed-UI sync still has one strict Dock truth
185	  path, but it is no longer the root accessibility string.
186	
187	## What Should Be Deleted Or Replaced
188	
189	The final plan must include a real retirement list, not just additions.
190	
191	Delete or replace:
192	
193	- `DockView.dockScreenValue` all-row `rowValues=` construction.
194	- `DisplayedUICaptureSupport.dockRowsFromRootValue(...)` as the only row truth
195	  parser.
196	- README/docs claims that Dock row identity/order are read from Dock root
197	  `rowValues=`.
198	- Any UI test assumption that a normal visible accessibility value should carry
199	  all Dock rows.
200	- Any per-call/manual publish filtering outside the central publish gate.
201	
202	Keep:
203	
204	- Stable `AutomationID.Dock.row(...)` identifiers on row views.
205	- Per-row `accessibilityValue(row.automationValue)` if profiling proves it is
206	  viewport-bounded and does not force all-row work.
207	- Existing `RenderCoalescer` if the central pipeline can absorb it cleanly.
208	- Existing `DockCardProjection` semantics unless model consensus finds a simpler
209	  owner split.
210	
211	## Open Questions For Consensus
212	
213	- Should automation proof move to a simulator-only file snapshot, a hidden
214	  paged accessibility snapshot, or another existing proof channel?
215	- Should the first implementation keep all projected row models in
216	  `DockScreenModel`, or introduce explicit viewport/window state now?
217	- Does publish gating belong in `DockStore`, `DockScreenStore`, or a new
218	  `DockRenderPipeline` object that owns both projection and equality?
219	- Which existing instrumentation should stay as permanent regression telemetry,
220	  and which should be deleted after the fix?
221	- What is the exact minimal deletion/migration path so there is never both an
222	  old root `rowValues` oracle and a new automation oracle active long-term?
223	
224	## Current Best Bet Before Consensus
225	
226	The smallest elegant fix is probably:
227	
228	1. Move all publish eligibility into one `DockRenderPipeline`.
229	2. Add display fingerprints and skip unchanged rendered projections.
230	3. Replace root `rowValues=` with a test-mode `DockAutomationSnapshotStore`.
231	4. Keep UI state as normal SwiftUI row arrays for now.
232	5. Add explicit performance-budget tests so no future feature can put all-row
233	   payloads back into body/accessibility work.
234	
235	This bet is intentionally provisional. The model-consensus pass must critique
236	it against the repo evidence and either simplify it or replace it.
237	
238	## Iteration Log
239

# Dock Lightning-Fast Architecture Fix Plan - 2026-06-04

## Status

Version: `v0`

This is a living architecture plan. It is intentionally not an implementation
patch. The first version captures the current evidence and the target shape so
the model-consensus pass can critique and simplify it.

Required external review gates:

- `$model-consensus` with `opus 4.8 max` and `gpt 5.5 xhigh`.
- `$fresh-consult` with Cursor Agent `composer-2.5-fast`.
- Do not implement in this pass.

## Source Evidence

Primary diagnostic input:

- `docs/IPHONE_17_PRO_DOCK_LAG_PROFILE_WORKLOG_2026-06-04.md`

Key measured facts:

- At `1,247` loaded Dock rows, `DockView.dockScreenValue` builds a `469,211`
  character accessibility payload in `20-22 ms`, repeatedly.
- The same runtime window logs frame hitches up to `103 ms`.
- `home` alone reproduces the hitch pattern at `978` rows; `M5` alone is much
  smoother at `269` rows.
- The data/projection pipeline is measurable but not the dominant visible cost:
  steady-state `dock.render.project` averaged `8 ms`,
  `dock.data_engine.snapshot` averaged `9 ms`, and `dock.main_publish` averaged
  `1 ms` in the final simulator proof.
- Untouched idle app runtime still rebuilt the full Dock root payload on host
  heartbeat/update publishes.

Relevant owner paths:

- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`
- `CodexDock/Dock/DockScreenStore.swift`
- `CodexDock/Dock/DockRenderProjector.swift`
- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`
- `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`
- `CodexDockUITests/DisplayedUICaptureSupport.swift`
- `README.md`

## Problem Statement

The Dock has crossed a boundary where normal screen updates can no longer carry
test/proof payloads or all-row derived state through SwiftUI body evaluation.
The current architecture lets a single host heartbeat trigger a full combined
Dock publish. That publish invalidates SwiftUI, and the Dock header computes a
root accessibility value that includes every rendered row's automation value.

The visible symptom is scroll lag, but the architecture problem is broader:
high-frequency data events are allowed to force large main-thread UI work that
is proportional to total row count.

## Target Architecture

The target is a Dock screen contract where user interaction cost is bounded by
visible UI, not by total Dock dataset size.

Performance guarantees:

- Main-thread work on heartbeat/no-visible-change events is `O(1)` or skipped.
- Main-thread work on a visible row update is proportional to the changed visible
  rows, not all rows.
- Scroll-time work is bounded by the viewport and nearby lazy rows.
- Test/proof extraction never runs as a normal SwiftUI accessibility value.
- Automation state is still deterministic, structured, and strict enough to
  catch UI drift.
- The architecture has one owner for publish eligibility and one owner for
  automation snapshots, so future code cannot reintroduce bulk payloads in view
  bodies.

## Proposed Shape For Model Critique

Create a central `DockRenderPipeline` concept owned by the Dock screen layer.
It should replace ad hoc "publish every combined snapshot" behavior with a
single place that decides whether a new host event changes the rendered Dock
screen.

The pipeline has three products:

1. `DockScreenModel`: small, Equatable, main-actor state for SwiftUI.
2. `DockRenderDataset`: off-main full-row data used by projection, search,
   filters, grouping, and details.
3. `DockAutomationSnapshot`: structured, on-demand proof data for UI tests and
   sync scripts.

The important rule: `DockView` can render `DockScreenModel`, but it must not
derive all-row automation payloads from body evaluation.

## Central Patterns To Introduce

### 1. Publish Gate

Add a single publish gate before `DockScreenStore` emits `.loaded`.

Inputs:

- Current rendered screen fingerprint.
- Next host snapshot metadata.
- Next combined projection fingerprint.
- Pending local UI overlays such as optimistic renames.
- Current projection options: lens, search, filters, collapsed groups.

Outputs:

- `skip`: no visible or automation-relevant screen change.
- `metadataOnly`: update connectivity/status side channels without invalidating
  the Dock row tree.
- `publish`: emit a new `DockScreenModel`.

The gate should reject heartbeat-only publishes when the ordered visible row IDs
and row display fingerprints are unchanged.

### 2. Stable Row Display Fingerprints

Each `DockRowViewModel` needs a compact fingerprint that represents only fields
that can change rendered row UI or row automation truth:

- identity: host, source host, projection ID, thread ID
- display ordering key
- status/origin/relationship
- repository, branch, label presence, color rail
- summary/title/last activity text used on the row
- pin state and pinned ordering fields

The fingerprint is the comparison primitive. The UI should not diff whole
payload strings.

### 3. Viewport-Bounded SwiftUI Contract

Keep `LazyVStack`, but make the state SwiftUI observes smaller:

- `DockScreenModel` contains summary/header/filter state, visible row section
  identities, and row view models needed for the current projection.
- Rows remain individually identified by stable row identity.
- Expensive all-row proof data and full encoded `rowValues` do not live in
  `DockView`.

The plan should decide whether `DockScreenModel` still carries all projected
rows for `LazyVStack` or whether it introduces an indexed collection/view model
that supports viewport-window extraction. The default preference is minimal:
first remove bulk accessibility work and no-op publishes, then add true windowing
only if profiling still shows total-row render cost.

### 4. Automation Snapshot Service

Replace Dock root `rowValues=` with a centralized test/proof path.

Candidate shape:

- `DockAutomationSnapshotStore` owned next to `DockScreenStore`.
- It receives accepted `DockRenderSnapshot` values off the main interaction path.
- It exposes compact screen state on the root accessibility value:
  `loaded; rows=1247; visibleRows=1247; revision=26; automationSnapshot=26`.
- UI tests and simulator proof scripts fetch full row proof data through a
  dedicated, explicitly test-only route.

The route could be:

- A hidden accessibility element with paged/chunked row payloads created only
  when `CODEX_DOCK_UI_TESTING=1`.
- A simulator-only app-container JSON snapshot written by the app when
  `CODEX_DOCK_UI_TESTING=1`.
- A local app diagnostic endpoint only in UI-test launch mode.

The model-consensus pass must choose the smallest robust route and specify how
scripts/tests migrate.

### 5. Performance Budget Tests

Add tests that fail when regressions reappear:

- Unit test the publish gate: heartbeat/no-row-change does not publish.
- Unit test row fingerprints: display-relevant changes publish; invisible
  metadata-only changes do not.
- Unit test root accessibility value length stays bounded at high row count.
- UI performance proof: with 1,200+ rows and both hosts, no all-row
  accessibility rebuilds occur during idle/scroll.
- Contract proof migration: displayed-UI sync still has one strict Dock truth
  path, but it is no longer the root accessibility string.

## What Should Be Deleted Or Replaced

The final plan must include a real retirement list, not just additions.

Delete or replace:

- `DockView.dockScreenValue` all-row `rowValues=` construction.
- `DisplayedUICaptureSupport.dockRowsFromRootValue(...)` as the only row truth
  parser.
- README/docs claims that Dock row identity/order are read from Dock root
  `rowValues=`.
- Any UI test assumption that a normal visible accessibility value should carry
  all Dock rows.
- Any per-call/manual publish filtering outside the central publish gate.

Keep:

- Stable `AutomationID.Dock.row(...)` identifiers on row views.
- Per-row `accessibilityValue(row.automationValue)` if profiling proves it is
  viewport-bounded and does not force all-row work.
- Existing `RenderCoalescer` if the central pipeline can absorb it cleanly.
- Existing `DockCardProjection` semantics unless model consensus finds a simpler
  owner split.

## Open Questions For Consensus

- Should automation proof move to a simulator-only file snapshot, a hidden
  paged accessibility snapshot, or another existing proof channel?
- Should the first implementation keep all projected row models in
  `DockScreenModel`, or introduce explicit viewport/window state now?
- Does publish gating belong in `DockStore`, `DockScreenStore`, or a new
  `DockRenderPipeline` object that owns both projection and equality?
- Which existing instrumentation should stay as permanent regression telemetry,
  and which should be deleted after the fix?
- What is the exact minimal deletion/migration path so there is never both an
  old root `rowValues` oracle and a new automation oracle active long-term?

## Current Best Bet Before Consensus

The smallest elegant fix is probably:

1. Move all publish eligibility into one `DockRenderPipeline`.
2. Add display fingerprints and skip unchanged rendered projections.
3. Replace root `rowValues=` with a test-mode `DockAutomationSnapshotStore`.
4. Keep UI state as normal SwiftUI row arrays for now.
5. Add explicit performance-budget tests so no future feature can put all-row
   payloads back into body/accessibility work.

This bet is intentionally provisional. The model-consensus pass must critique
it against the repo evidence and either simplify it or replace it.

version is not approved. Next step is independent `$model-consensus` with

32	3. `DockDataEngine.apply(snapshot, host:)` replaces that host's card array.

38	   a detached task.
39	7. The `RenderCoalescer` drops superseded revisions and yields the newest
40	   render snapshot.
41	8. `DockScreenStore.start()` assigns `state = .loaded(renderSnapshot)` on the
42	   main actor.
43	9. SwiftUI renders the Dock rows.

# iPhone 17 Pro Dock Lag Profile Worklog - 2026-06-04

## Scope

Diagnose severe UI lag on Amir's iPhone 17 Pro when Codex Dock is connected to
both the M5 relay and the home relay. The lag is especially visible while
scrolling, but it is also noticeable across normal app interactions.

This pass is diagnosis only. Do not apply performance repairs in this worklog's
scope. Instrumentation should be easy to disable for real builds and should not
log secrets, prompt text, transcript text, raw JSON-RPC payloads, bearer tokens,
or `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

## Known Device And Host Context

- Device: iPhone 17 Pro,
  `CB9FFF0E-89AD-57B5-9C00-6552D814875E`
- Last known installed build before this profiling pass: `20260604163222`
- Expected device hosts:
  - `amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`

## 2026-06-04T16:42:14Z - Initial Code-Path Findings

The main Dock screen pipeline is a multi-stage path:

1. Each configured host has a `StreamReconciler`.
2. Each host snapshot reaches `DockStore.handleReconcilerSnapshot`.
3. `DockDataEngine.apply(snapshot, host:)` replaces that host's card array.
4. `DockDataEngine.snapshot(now:)` builds one combined Dock snapshot across
   hosts.
5. `DockStore.publishSnapshot()` publishes that combined snapshot to
   `DockScreenStore`.
6. `DockScreenStore.enqueueProjection(snapshot:)` moves render projection onto
   a detached task.
7. The `RenderCoalescer` drops superseded revisions and yields the newest
   render snapshot.
8. `DockScreenStore.start()` assigns `state = .loaded(renderSnapshot)` on the
   main actor.
9. SwiftUI renders the Dock rows.

- Main-actor publish may still be too heavy if SwiftUI receives large, frequent

The Dock screen uses an outer `ScrollView` and nested `LazyVStack` sections for
rows, pinned rows, grouped rows, and host status rows. It does not use `List` for
the main Dock surface.

That matters because each `DockScreenStore.state = .loaded(renderSnapshot)`
assignment can invalidate SwiftUI's view tree while the user is scrolling. If
host snapshots arrive frequently, a detached data projection is not enough by
itself; the final main-actor state replacement may still interrupt scrolling.

value for the Dock root by collecting automation data from visible rows. In the
newest lens this can walk all projected rows, encode each row's automation
value, and concatenate the result. This is useful for tests, but on device it
may amplify the cost of every loaded-state render. This is a suspected cost
only, not yet proven.

370	    final class ProbeView: UIView {
371	        weak var coordinator: Coordinator?
372	
373	        override init(frame: CGRect) {
374	            super.init(frame: frame)
375	            isUserInteractionEnabled = false
376	            isAccessibilityElement = false
377	        }
378	
379	        required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
380	            super.init(coder: coder)
381	            isUserInteractionEnabled = false
382	            isAccessibilityElement = false
383	        }
384	
385	        override func didMoveToSuperview() {
386	            super.didMoveToSuperview()
387	            coordinator?.scheduleAttachmentAttempts(from: self)
388	        }
389	
390	        override func didMoveToWindow() {
391	            super.didMoveToWindow()
392	            coordinator?.scheduleAttachmentAttempts(from: self)
393	        }
394	    }
395	
396	    @MainActor
397	    final class Coordinator: NSObject {
398	        private weak var scrollView: UIScrollView?
399	        private var observation: NSKeyValueObservation?
400	        private var attachmentAttempts = 0
401	
402	        deinit {
403	            observation?.invalidate()
404	        }
405	
406	        func scheduleAttachmentAttempts(from view: UIView) {
407	            attach(from: view)
408	            for delay in [0.05, 0.2, 0.6, 1.2, 2.5, 5.0] {
409	                DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + delay) { [weak self, weak view] in
410	                    guard let self, let view else {
411	                        return
412	                    }
413	                    self.attach(from: view)
414	                }
415	            }
416	        }
417	
418	        func attach(from view: UIView) {
419	            attachmentAttempts += 1
420	            guard let scrollView = observedScrollView(for: view),
421	                  self.scrollView !== scrollView else {
422	                return
423	            }
424	            observation?.invalidate()
425	            self.scrollView = scrollView
426	            PerformanceProbe.dockScrollObserverAttached(
427	                attempt: attachmentAttempts,
428	                offsetY: Double(scrollView.contentOffset.y),
429	                contentHeight: Double(scrollView.contentSize.height),
430	                boundsHeight: Double(scrollView.bounds.height),
431	                adjustedTopInset: Double(scrollView.adjustedContentInset.top),
432	                adjustedBottomInset: Double(scrollView.adjustedContentInset.bottom)
433	            )
434	            observation = scrollView.observe(\.contentOffset, options: [.new]) { scrollView, _ in
435	                Task { @MainActor in
436	                    PerformanceProbe.dockScrollOffsetChanged(
437	                        offsetY: Double(scrollView.contentOffset.y),
438	                        contentHeight: Double(scrollView.contentSize.height),
439	                        boundsHeight: Double(scrollView.bounds.height)
440	                    )
441	                }
442	            }
443	        }
444	
445	        private func observedScrollView(for view: UIView) -> UIScrollView? {
446	            let enclosing = enclosingScrollView(for: view)
447	            let largestScrollable = view.window.map { window in
448	                scrollViews(in: window)
449	                    .filter { isScrollable($0) }
450	                    .max { lhs, rhs in
451	                        lhs.contentSize.height < rhs.contentSize.height
452	                    }
453	            } ?? nil
454	            return largestScrollable ?? enclosing
455	        }
456	
457	        private func isScrollable(_ scrollView: UIScrollView) -> Bool {
458	            let scrollableHeight = scrollView.contentSize.height
459	                + scrollView.adjustedContentInset.top
460	                + scrollView.adjustedContentInset.bottom
461	                - scrollView.bounds.height
462	            return scrollableHeight > 24
463	        }
464	
465	        private func enclosingScrollView(for view: UIView) -> UIScrollView? {
466	            var current = view.superview
467	            while let candidate = current {
468	                if let scrollView = candidate as? UIScrollView {
469	                    return scrollView
470	                }
471	                current = candidate.superview
472	            }
473	            return nil
474	        }
475	
476	        private func scrollViews(in view: UIView) -> [UIScrollView] {
477	            var matches: [UIScrollView] = []
478	            if let scrollView = view as? UIScrollView {
479	                matches.append(scrollView)
480	            }
481	            for subview in view.subviews {
482	                matches.append(contentsOf: scrollViews(in: subview))
483	            }
484	            return matches
485	        }
486	    }
487	}

3	public actor RenderCoalescer<Snapshot: Sendable> {
4	    public let snapshots: AsyncStream<Snapshot>
5	
6	    private let continuation: AsyncStream<Snapshot>.Continuation
7	    private var latestAcceptedRevision: RenderRevision?
8	
9	    public init(
10	        bufferingNewest: Int = CodexDockConstants.Rendering.renderStreamBufferNewest
11	    ) {
12	        let stream = AsyncStream.makeStream(
13	            of: Snapshot.self,
14	            bufferingPolicy: .bufferingNewest(bufferingNewest)
15	        )
16	        self.snapshots = stream.stream
17	        self.continuation = stream.continuation
18	    }
19	
20	    public func submit(_ snapshot: Snapshot, revision: RenderRevision) {
21	        if let latestAcceptedRevision,
22	           revision < latestAcceptedRevision {
23	            PerformanceProbe.event(
24	                "render.coalescer.drop_stale",
25	                fields: [
26	                    "revision": "\(revision.rawValue)",
27	                    "latest_revision": "\(latestAcceptedRevision.rawValue)",
28	                ]
29	            )
30	            return
31	        }
32	
33	        latestAcceptedRevision = revision
34	        let result = continuation.yield(snapshot)
35	        PerformanceProbe.event(
36	            "render.coalescer.submit",
37	            fields: [
38	                "revision": "\(revision.rawValue)",
39	                "yield_result": "\(result)",
40	            ]
41	        )
42	    }
43	
44	    public func stream() -> AsyncStream<Snapshot> {
45	        snapshots
46	    }
47	
48	    public func latestRevision() -> RenderRevision? {
49	        latestAcceptedRevision
50	    }
51	
52	    public func finish() {
53	        continuation.finish()
54	    }
55	}

3	struct DockRenderProjector: Sendable {
4	    let now: @Sendable () -> Date
5	
6	    init(now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = Date.init) {
7	        self.now = now
8	    }
9	
10	    func snapshot(
11	        from input: DockRenderInput,
12	        localMetadata: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
13	    ) -> DockSnapshot {
14	        let startedAt = Date()
15	        let rowProjector = ThreadCardRowProjector(
16	            hosts: input.hosts,
17	            hostIdentityResolver: input.hostIdentityResolver,
18	            localMetadata: localMetadata,
19	            now: now
20	        )
21	        let liveRows = input.hosts.flatMap { host in
22	            rowProjector.rows(
23	                from: input.cardsByHostID[host.id] ?? [],
24	                configuredHostID: host.id
25	            )
26	        }
27	        // Local metadata may decorate relay rows, but it must never create card
28	        // rows. The relay is the single source of truth for card existence and order.
29	
30	        let snapshot = DockSnapshot(
31	            host: DockHostViewModel(host: input.hosts[0]),
32	            hosts: input.hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init),
33	            hostStates: input.hostStates,
34	            hostIdentityResolver: input.hostIdentityResolver,
35	            rows: liveRows,
36	            isPartial: input.isPartial
37	        )
38	        if PerformanceProbe.isEnabled {
39	            let hostCardCounts = input.hosts
40	                .map { "\($0.id):\(input.cardsByHostID[$0.id]?.count ?? 0)" }
41	                .joined(separator: ",")
42	            PerformanceProbe.event(
43	                "dock.snapshot.project",
44	                fields: [
45	                    "hosts": "\(input.hosts.count)",
46	                    "host_cards": hostCardCounts,
47	                    "rows": "\(snapshot.rows.count)",
48	                    "metadata_entries": "\(localMetadata.count)",
49	                    "partial": "\(snapshot.isPartial)",
50	                    "duration_ms": "\(PerformanceProbe.milliseconds(since: startedAt))",
51	                ]
52	            )
53	        }
54	        return snapshot
55	    }
56	
57	    func render(
58	        snapshot: DockSnapshot,
59	        options: DockProjectionOptions,
60	        revision: RenderRevision
61	    ) -> DockRenderSnapshot {
62	        let startedAt = Date()
63	        let renderSnapshot = DockRenderSnapshot(
64	            revision: revision,
65	            snapshot: snapshot,
66	            projection: snapshot.project(options: options)
67	        )
68	        if PerformanceProbe.isEnabled {
69	            PerformanceProbe.event(
70	                "dock.render.project",
71	                fields: [
72	                    "revision": "\(revision.rawValue)",
73	                    "rows": "\(snapshot.rows.count)",

78	                    "duration_ms": "\(PerformanceProbe.milliseconds(since: startedAt))",
79	                ]

		set -eu; \
		udid="$$(python3 scripts/sim.py resolve "$(SIM)")"; \
		output_dir="$(SIM_UI_CLIENT_RENAME_DIR)"; \
		mkdir -p "$$output_dir" "$(APP_BUILD_LOG_DIR)"; \

		sim_ready_host="$$output_dir/client-rename-fixture-ready-simulator.json"; \
		host_ready="/tmp/codex-client/codex-dock-client-rename-proof-ready.json"; \
		sim_ready="/tmp/codex-client/codex-dock-client-rename-proof-ready.json"; \
		sim_ui_result="/tmp/codex-client/codex-dock-client-rename-latency-ui.json"; \
		build_log="$(APP_BUILD_LOG_DIR)/sim-ui-client-rename-build-$(APP_BUILD_NUMBER).log"; \
		test_log="$(APP_BUILD_LOG_DIR)/sim-ui-client-rename-test-$(APP_BUILD_NUMBER).log"; \

		xcrun simctl spawn "$$udid" /bin/rm -f "$$sim_ready" "$$sim_ui_result" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; \
		echo "resetting simulator app data for client rename latency proof"; \

		echo "building client rename latency proof test for $(APP_SCHEME) on simulator $$udid build $(APP_BUILD_NUMBER)"; \

			echo "client rename proof build failed; see $$build_log" >&2; \
			tail -n 80 "$$build_log" >&2; \
			exit 1; \
		fi; \
		fixture_pid=""; \
		cleanup() { \
			status="$${1:-$$?}"; \
			touch "$$fixture_stop" 2>/dev/null || true; \
			rm -f "$$host_ready"; \
			xcrun simctl spawn "$$udid" /bin/rm -f "$$sim_ready" "$$sim_ui_result" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; \
			if [ -n "$${fixture_pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$$fixture_pid" 2>/dev/null; then \

				wait "$$fixture_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; \
			fi; \
			exit "$$status"; \

			copy_sim_ui_result() { \
				if [ -f "$$ui_result" ]; then return 0; fi; \
				tmp="$$ui_result.tmp"; \
				for candidate in "$$sim_ui_result" "$$ui_result"; do \
					if xcrun simctl spawn "$$udid" /bin/cat "$$candidate" > "$$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then \
						mv "$$tmp" "$$ui_result"; \
						return 0; \
					fi; \
				done; \
				rm -f "$$tmp"; \
				return 1; \
			}; \
		trap cleanup INT TERM; \
		echo "starting client rename latency fixture"; \
		rtk node scripts/dock-relay-client-rename-latency-fixture.mjs --ready-out "$$fixture_ready" --ui-result-in "$$ui_result" --stop-in "$$fixture_stop" --json-out "$$report_json" --summary-out "$$report_md" --server-ack-delay-ms "$(SIM_UI_CLIENT_RENAME_SERVER_ACK_DELAY_MS)" --ui-budget-ms "$(SIM_UI_CLIENT_RENAME_UI_BUDGET_MS)" --wait-timeout-ms "$(SIM_UI_SYNC_READY_TIMEOUT_MS)" > "$$fixture_log" 2>&1 & \
		fixture_pid="$$!"; \
		deadline=$$(( $$(date +%s) + ( $(SIM_UI_SYNC_READY_TIMEOUT_MS) / 1000 ) )); \
		while [ ! -f "$$fixture_ready" ]; do \
			if ! kill -0 "$$fixture_pid" 2>/dev/null; then \
				echo "client rename fixture exited before ready; see $$fixture_log" >&2; \
				tail -n 120 "$$fixture_log" >&2; \
				cleanup 1; \
			fi; \
			if [ "$$(date +%s)" -gt "$$deadline" ]; then \
				echo "client rename fixture did not become ready; see $$fixture_log" >&2; \
				tail -n 120 "$$fixture_log" >&2; \
				cleanup 1; \
			fi; \
			sleep 0.2; \
		done; \
		cp "$$fixture_ready" "$$host_ready"; \
		rtk python3 -c "import json,sys; data=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); data[\"uiResultPath\"]=sys.argv[3]; open(sys.argv[2],\"w\").write(json.dumps(data)+\"\\n\")" "$$fixture_ready" "$$sim_ready_host" "$$sim_ui_result"; \
		xcrun simctl spawn "$$udid" /bin/mkdir -p /tmp/codex-client; \
		xcrun simctl spawn "$$udid" /bin/sh -c "/bin/cat > $$sim_ready" < "$$sim_ready_host"; \
		echo "running controlled client rename latency UI test on $(SIM)"; \
		test_status=0; \
			if ! CODEX_DOCK_CLIENT_RENAME_PROOF_UI_RESULT_HOST="$$ui_result" xcodebuild -quiet test-without-building -project CodexDock.xcodeproj -scheme "$(APP_SCHEME)" -destination "id=$$udid" -derivedDataPath "$(APP_DERIVED_DATA)" -only-testing:CodexDockUITests/CodexDockThreadRenameUITests/testControlledClientRenameIsOptimisticWhenConfigured > "$$test_log" 2>&1; then \
				test_status=1; \
			fi; \
		copy_sim_ui_result || true; \
		touch "$$fixture_stop"; \
		fixture_status=0; \
		if ! wait "$$fixture_pid"; then fixture_status=1; fi; \
		fixture_pid=""; \

		rm -f "$$host_ready"; \

			exit 1; \
		fi; \
		if [ "$$fixture_status" -ne 0 ]; then \
			echo "client rename latency fixture failed; see $$fixture_log" >&2; \
			tail -n 120 "$$fixture_log" >&2; \
			if [ -f "$$ui_result" ]; then echo "wrote $$ui_result"; fi; \
			if [ -f "$$report_json" ]; then echo "wrote $$report_json"; fi; \
			exit 1; \

1	# Dock Lightning-Fast Architecture Fix Plan - 2026-06-04
2	
3	## Status
4	
5	Version: `v0`
6	
7	This is a living architecture plan. It is intentionally not an implementation
8	patch. The first version captures the current evidence and the target shape so
9	the model-consensus pass can critique and simplify it.
10	
11	Required external review gates:
12	
13	- `$model-consensus` with `opus 4.8 max` and `gpt 5.5 xhigh`.
14	- `$fresh-consult` with Cursor Agent `composer-2.5-fast`.
15	- Do not implement in this pass.
16	
17	## Source Evidence
18	
19	Primary diagnostic input:
20	
21	- `docs/IPHONE_17_PRO_DOCK_LAG_PROFILE_WORKLOG_2026-06-04.md`
22	
23	Key measured facts:
24	
25	- At `1,247` loaded Dock rows, `DockView.dockScreenValue` builds a `469,211`
26	  character accessibility payload in `20-22 ms`, repeatedly.
27	- The same runtime window logs frame hitches up to `103 ms`.
28	- `home` alone reproduces the hitch pattern at `978` rows; `M5` alone is much
29	  smoother at `269` rows.
30	- The data/projection pipeline is measurable but not the dominant visible cost:
31	  steady-state `dock.render.project` averaged `8 ms`,
32	  `dock.data_engine.snapshot` averaged `9 ms`, and `dock.main_publish` averaged
33	  `1 ms` in the final simulator proof.
34	- Untouched idle app runtime still rebuilt the full Dock root payload on host
35	  heartbeat/update publishes.
36	
37	Relevant owner paths:
38	
39	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`
40	- `CodexDock/Dock/DockScreenStore.swift`
41	- `CodexDock/Dock/DockRenderProjector.swift`
42	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`
43	- `CodexDock/State/DockCardProjection.swift`
44	- `CodexDockUITests/DisplayedUICaptureSupport.swift`
45	- `README.md`
46	
47	## Problem Statement
48	
49	The Dock has crossed a boundary where normal screen updates can no longer carry
50	test/proof payloads or all-row derived state through SwiftUI body evaluation.
51	The current architecture lets a single host heartbeat trigger a full combined
52	Dock publish. That publish invalidates SwiftUI, and the Dock header computes a
53	root accessibility value that includes every rendered row's automation value.
54	
55	The visible symptom is scroll lag, but the architecture problem is broader:
56	high-frequency data events are allowed to force large main-thread UI work that
57	is proportional to total row count.
58	
59	## Target Architecture
60	
61	The target is a Dock screen contract where user interaction cost is bounded by
62	visible UI, not by total Dock dataset size.
63	
64	Performance guarantees:
65	
66	- Main-thread work on heartbeat/no-visible-change events is `O(1)` or skipped.
67	- Main-thread work on a visible row update is proportional to the changed visible
68	  rows, not all rows.
69	- Scroll-time work is bounded by the viewport and nearby lazy rows.
70	- Test/proof extraction never runs as a normal SwiftUI accessibility value.
71	- Automation state is still deterministic, structured, and strict enough to
72	  catch UI drift.
73	- The architecture has one owner for publish eligibility and one owner for
74	  automation snapshots, so future code cannot reintroduce bulk payloads in view
75	  bodies.
76	
77	## Proposed Shape For Model Critique
78	
79	Create a central `DockRenderPipeline` concept owned by the Dock screen layer.
80	It should replace ad hoc "publish every combined snapshot" behavior with a
81	single place that decides whether a new host event changes the rendered Dock
82	screen.
83	
84	The pipeline has three products:
85	
86	1. `DockScreenModel`: small, Equatable, main-actor state for SwiftUI.
87	2. `DockRenderDataset`: off-main full-row data used by projection, search,
88	   filters, grouping, and details.
89	3. `DockAutomationSnapshot`: structured, on-demand proof data for UI tests and
90	   sync scripts.
91	
92	The important rule: `DockView` can render `DockScreenModel`, but it must not
93	derive all-row automation payloads from body evaluation.
94	
95	## Central Patterns To Introduce
96	
97	### 1. Publish Gate
98	
99	Add a single publish gate before `DockScreenStore` emits `.loaded`.
100	
101	Inputs:
102	
103	- Current rendered screen fingerprint.
104	- Next host snapshot metadata.
105	- Next combined projection fingerprint.
106	- Pending local UI overlays such as optimistic renames.
107	- Current projection options: lens, search, filters, collapsed groups.
108	
109	Outputs:
110	
111	- `skip`: no visible or automation-relevant screen change.
112	- `metadataOnly`: update connectivity/status side channels without invalidating
113	  the Dock row tree.
114	- `publish`: emit a new `DockScreenModel`.
115	
116	The gate should reject heartbeat-only publishes when the ordered visible row IDs
117	and row display fingerprints are unchanged.
118	
119	### 2. Stable Row Display Fingerprints
120	
121	Each `DockRowViewModel` needs a compact fingerprint that represents only fields
122	that can change rendered row UI or row automation truth:
123	
124	- identity: host, source host, projection ID, thread ID
125	- display ordering key
126	- status/origin/relationship
127	- repository, branch, label presence, color rail
128	- summary/title/last activity text used on the row
129	- pin state and pinned ordering fields
130	
131	The fingerprint is the comparison primitive. The UI should not diff whole
132	payload strings.
133	
134	### 3. Viewport-Bounded SwiftUI Contract
135	
136	Keep `LazyVStack`, but make the state SwiftUI observes smaller:
137	
138	- `DockScreenModel` contains summary/header/filter state, visible row section
139	  identities, and row view models needed for the current projection.
140	- Rows remain individually identified by stable row identity.
141	- Expensive all-row proof data and full encoded `rowValues` do not live in
142	  `DockView`.
143	
144	The plan should decide whether `DockScreenModel` still carries all projected
145	rows for `LazyVStack` or whether it introduces an indexed collection/view model
146	that supports viewport-window extraction. The default preference is minimal:
147	first remove bulk accessibility work and no-op publishes, then add true windowing
148	only if profiling still shows total-row render cost.
149	
150	### 4. Automation Snapshot Service

3	struct ThreadCardRowProjector {
4	    let hosts: [DockHostConfiguration]
5	    let hostIdentityResolver: DockHostIdentityResolver
6	    let localMetadata: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
7	    let now: @Sendable () -> Date
8	
9	    private struct ProjectionStats {
10	        var filteredOutCount = 0
11	        var exactMetadataHits = 0
12	        var fallbackMetadataHits = 0
13	        var fallbackMetadataMisses = 0
14	    }
15	
16	    func rows(
17	        from cards: [DockThreadCardDTO],
18	        configuredHostID: String? = nil
19	    ) -> [DockRowViewModel] {
20	        let startedAt = Date()
21	        var stats = ProjectionStats()
22	        let rows = cards.compactMap { card -> DockRowViewModel? in
23	            guard card.isAppFacingHumanThreadCard else {
24	                stats.filteredOutCount += 1
25	                return nil
26	            }
27	            return makeRow(card: card, stats: &stats)
28	        }
29	        if PerformanceProbe.isEnabled {
30	            PerformanceProbe.event(
31	                "dock.rows.project",
32	                fields: [
33	                    "configured_host_id": configuredHostID ?? "none",
34	                    "cards": "\(cards.count)",
35	                    "rows": "\(rows.count)",
36	                    "filtered_out": "\(stats.filteredOutCount)",
37	                    "metadata_entries": "\(localMetadata.count)",
38	                    "metadata_exact_hits": "\(stats.exactMetadataHits)",
39	                    "metadata_fallback_hits": "\(stats.fallbackMetadataHits)",
40	                    "metadata_fallback_misses": "\(stats.fallbackMetadataMisses)",
41	                    "duration_ms": "\(PerformanceProbe.milliseconds(since: startedAt))",
42	                ]
43	            )
44	        }
45	        return rows
46	    }
47	
48	    func makeRow(card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> DockRowViewModel {
49	        var stats = ProjectionStats()
50	        return makeRow(card: card, stats: &stats)
51	    }
52	
53	    private func makeRow(
54	        card: DockThreadCardDTO,
55	        stats: inout ProjectionStats
56	    ) -> DockRowViewModel {
57	        guard let resolvedSourceHostID = nonEmpty(card.sourceHostID),
58	              let projectionID = nonEmpty(card.projectionID),
59	              let displayOrderKey = nonEmpty(card.displayOrderKey) else {
60	            preconditionFailure("ThreadCardRowProjector only accepts relay projection rows with sourceHostID, projectionID, and displayOrderKey")
61	        }
62	        // Dock rows are projection rows. `logicalHostID` is display payload only;
63	        // action identity follows the relay-owned source host namespace.
64	        let id = HostScopedThreadID(hostID: resolvedSourceHostID, threadID: card.threadID)
65	        let metadata = metadata(
66	            for: id,
67	            backendSessionID: card.backendSessionID,
68	            sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID,
69	            stats: &stats
70	        )
71	        let activityDate = activityDate(for: card)
72	        return DockRowViewModel(
73	            threadIdentity: id,
74	            sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID,
75	            projectionID: projectionID,
76	            backendSessionID: card.backendSessionID,
77	            title: nonEmpty(card.title) ?? "Thread \(shortThreadID(card.threadID))",
78	            hostDisplayName: nonEmpty(card.hostDisplayName)
79	                ?? hostDisplayName(for: card.logicalHostID, sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID),
80	            hostEndpoint: nonEmpty(card.hostEndpoint)
81	                ?? hostEndpoint(for: card.logicalHostID, sourceHostID: resolvedSourceHostID),
82	            repository: nonEmpty(card.repository) ?? nonEmpty(card.workingDirectory) ?? "Unknown workspace",
83	            branch: nonEmpty(card.branch) ?? "No branch",
84	            status: status(for: card.status),
85	            lastActivity: relativeTime(since: activityDate),
86	            lastActivityDate: activityDate,
87	            displayOrderKey: displayOrderKey,
88	            summary: nonEmpty(card.displaySummary) ?? "No summary",
89	            rail: metadata?.rail ?? rail(for: card),
90	            label: metadata?.label,
91	            origin: origin(for: card),
92	            relationship: relationship(for: card),
93	            isPinned: metadata?.isPinned ?? false,
94	            pinnedAt: metadata?.pinnedAt,
95	            pinnedOrder: metadata?.pinnedOrder
96	        )
97	    }
98	
99	    private func metadata(
100	        for id: HostScopedThreadID,
101	        backendSessionID: String,
102	        sourceHostID: String?,
103	        stats: inout ProjectionStats
104	    ) -> LocalThreadMetadata? {
105	        let exactKey = LocalThreadMetadataKey(
106	            hostID: id.hostID,
107	            backendSessionID: backendSessionID,
108	            threadID: id.threadID
109	        )
110	        if let metadata = localMetadata[exactKey] {
111	            stats.exactMetadataHits += 1
112	            return metadata
113	        }
114	
115	        let fallback = localMetadata.first { key, _ in
116	            guard key.backendSessionID == backendSessionID,
117	                  key.threadID == id.threadID else {
118	                return false
119	            }
120	            return hostIdentityResolver.logicalHostID(
121	                forAlias: key.hostID,
122	                sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceHostID
123	            ) == id.hostID
124	        }?.value
125	        if fallback == nil {
126	            stats.fallbackMetadataMisses += 1
127	        } else {
128	            stats.fallbackMetadataHits += 1
129	        }
130	        return fallback
131	    }
132	
133	    private func activityDate(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> Date {
134	        // The relay owns card recency. If this timestamp is missing, decoding
135	        // fails at the DTO boundary instead of letting Swift invent an order.
136	        Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval(card.activityAtMs) / 1_000)
137	    }
138	
139	    private func status(for status: DockThreadCardStatus) -> DockRowStatusKind {
140	        switch status {
141	        case .running:
142	            return .running
143	        case .needsInput:
144	            return .needsInput
145	        case .needsApproval:
146	            return .needsApproval
147	        case .idle:
148	            return .idle
149	        case .error:
150	            return .error
151	        case .dormant:
152	            return .dormant
153	        case .unknown:
154	            return .unknown
155	        }
156	    }
157	
158	    private func origin(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> SessionOrigin {
159	        switch card.lane {
160	        case .human:
161	            return .humanInteractive(subtype: .cli)
162	        case .agent:
163	            return .agentOrAutomation(subtype: .exec)
164	        case .unknown:
165	            switch card.sourceKind {
166	            case .human:
167	                return .humanInteractive(subtype: .cli)
168	            case .automation:
169	                return .agentOrAutomation(subtype: .exec)
170	            case .unknown:
171	                return .unknown()
172	            }
173	        }
174	    }
175	
176	    private func relativeTime(since date: Date) -> String {
177	        guard date != .distantPast else {
178	            return "No activity"
179	        }
180	        let seconds = max(0, Int(now().timeIntervalSince(date)))
181	
182	        switch seconds {
183	        case 0..<60:
184	            return "now"
185	        case 60..<3_600:
186	            return "\(seconds / 60)m ago"
187	        case 3_600..<86_400:
188	            return "\(seconds / 3_600)h ago"
189	        default:
190	            return "\(seconds / 86_400)d ago"
191	        }
192	    }
193	
194	    private func relationship(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> DockRowThreadRelationship {
195	        switch card.relationship {
196	        case .forked:
197	            return .forked
198	        case .root, .spawned:
199	            return .root
200	        case .unknown, nil:
201	            return .root
202	        }
203	    }
204	
205	    private func rail(for card: DockThreadCardDTO) -> DockRowRail {
206	        let rails = DockRowRail.allCases
207	        let checksum = card.threadID.utf8.reduce(UInt64(0)) { partial, byte in
208	            (partial &* 31) &+ UInt64(byte)
209	        }
210	        return rails[Int(checksum % UInt64(rails.count))]
211	    }
212	
213	    private func nonEmpty(_ value: String?) -> String? {
214	        let trimmed = value?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
215	        if let trimmed, !trimmed.isEmpty {
216	            return trimmed
217	        }
218	        return nil
219	    }
220	
221	    private func hostDisplayName(for hostID: String, sourceHostID: String? = nil) -> String {
222	        hostIdentityResolver.displayName(forAlias: hostID, sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceHostID)
223	            ?? hostID
224	    }
225	
226	    private func hostEndpoint(for hostID: String, sourceHostID: String? = nil) -> String {
227	        hostIdentityResolver.endpoint(forAlias: hostID, sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceHostID)
228	            ?? hostID
229	    }
230	
231	    private func shortThreadID(_ threadID: String) -> String {
232	        if threadID.count <= 12 {
233	            return threadID
234	        }
235	        return String(threadID.prefix(8))
236	    }
237	}

3	public protocol ThreadCardStreamConnection: Sendable {
4	    func subscribe() async throws -> ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO
5	    func resync() async throws -> ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO
6	    func updates() -> AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error>
7	    func close() async
8	}
9	
10	public protocol ThreadCardStreamConnecting: Sendable {
11	    func connect(to host: DockHostConfiguration) async throws -> any ThreadCardStreamConnection
12	}
13	
14	struct ThreadCardProjectionStreamConnector: ProjectionStreamConnecting {
15	    private let host: DockHostConfiguration
16	    private let streamClient: any ThreadCardStreamConnecting
17	
18	    init(
19	        host: DockHostConfiguration,
20	        streamClient: any ThreadCardStreamConnecting
21	    ) {
22	        self.host = host
23	        self.streamClient = streamClient
24	    }
25	
26	    func connect() async throws -> any ProjectionStreamConnection<DockThreadCardDTO> {
27	        let connection = try await streamClient.connect(to: host)
28	        return ThreadCardProjectionStreamConnection(connection: connection)
29	    }
30	}
31	
32	private actor ThreadCardProjectionStreamConnection: ProjectionStreamConnection {
33	    private let connection: any ThreadCardStreamConnection
34	    private let updateStream: AsyncThrowingStream<ProjectionEnvelope<DockThreadCardDTO>, Error>
35	    private let updateContinuation: AsyncThrowingStream<ProjectionEnvelope<DockThreadCardDTO>, Error>.Continuation
36	    private var updateTask: Task<Void, Never>?
37	
38	    init(connection: any ThreadCardStreamConnection) {
39	        self.connection = connection
40	        let stream = AsyncThrowingStream<ProjectionEnvelope<DockThreadCardDTO>, Error>.makeStream()
41	        self.updateStream = stream.stream
42	        self.updateContinuation = stream.continuation
43	        self.updateTask = Task { [connection, updateContinuation] in
44	            do {
45	                for try await update in connection.updates() {
46	                    updateContinuation.yield(ProjectionEnvelope(update))
47	                }
48	                updateContinuation.finish()
49	            } catch {
50	                updateContinuation.finish(throwing: error)
51	            }
52	        }
53	    }
54	
55	    deinit {
56	        updateTask?.cancel()
57	        updateContinuation.finish()
58	    }
59	
60	    func subscribe() async throws -> ProjectionEnvelope<DockThreadCardDTO> {
61	        ProjectionEnvelope(try await connection.subscribe())
62	    }
63	
64	    func resync(reason _: StreamReconcilerRecoveryReason) async throws -> ProjectionEnvelope<DockThreadCardDTO> {
65	        ProjectionEnvelope(try await connection.resync())
66	    }
67	
68	    nonisolated func updates() -> AsyncThrowingStream<ProjectionEnvelope<DockThreadCardDTO>, Error> {
69	        updateStream
70	    }
71	
72	    func close() async {
73	        updateTask?.cancel()
74	        updateContinuation.finish()
75	        await connection.close()
76	    }
77	}

79	public struct AppServerThreadCardStreamClient: ThreadCardStreamConnecting {
80	    private let view: ThreadCardStreamView
81	    private let makeClient: @Sendable (DockRelayEndpoint) -> AppServerClient
82	    private let observabilityStore: ClientObservabilityStore
83	    let defaultConnectionPolicy: AppServerConnectionPolicy?
84	
85	    public init(
86	        view: ThreadCardStreamView = .dock,
87	        observabilityStore: ClientObservabilityStore = .shared,
88	        connectionPolicy: AppServerConnectionPolicy = .oneShot
89	    ) {

91	        self.observabilityStore = observabilityStore
92	        self.defaultConnectionPolicy = connectionPolicy
93	        self.makeClient = { endpoint in
94	            AppServerClient(
95	                webSocketURL: endpoint.webSocketURL,
96	                bearerToken: nil,
97	                connectionPolicy: connectionPolicy
98	            )
99	        }
100	    }
101	
102	    public init(
103	        view: ThreadCardStreamView = .dock,
104	        observabilityStore: ClientObservabilityStore = .shared,
105	        makeClient: @escaping @Sendable (DockRelayEndpoint) -> AppServerClient
106	    ) {

113	    public func connect(to host: DockHostConfiguration) async throws -> any ThreadCardStreamConnection {
114	        let client = makeClient(host.endpoint)
115	        _ = try await client.connectAndInitialize(timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.connectInitializeTimeout)
116	        return AppServerThreadCardStreamConnection(

125	public actor AppServerThreadCardStreamConnection: ThreadCardStreamConnection {
126	    private let client: AppServerClient
127	    private let view: ThreadCardStreamView
128	    private let host: DockHostConfiguration
129	    private let observabilityStore: ClientObservabilityStore
130	    private let updateStream: AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error>
131	    private let updateContinuation: AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error>.Continuation
132	    private var notificationTask: Task<Void, Never>?
133	
134	    init(
135	        client: AppServerClient,
136	        view: ThreadCardStreamView = .dock,
137	        host: DockHostConfiguration,
138	        observabilityStore: ClientObservabilityStore = .shared
139	    ) {
140	        self.client = client
141	        self.view = view
142	        self.host = host
143	        self.observabilityStore = observabilityStore
144	        let stream = AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error>.makeStream()
145	        self.updateStream = stream.stream
146	        self.updateContinuation = stream.continuation
147	        let updateRoute = Self.updateRoute(for: view)
148	        self.notificationTask = Task { [client, updateContinuation, host, observabilityStore, updateRoute] in
149	            for await notification in client.notifications {
150	                guard notification.method == updateRoute else {
151	                    continue
152	                }
153	                await observabilityStore.recordPassive(
154	                    route: updateRoute,
155	                    configuredHostID: host.id,
156	                    relayHostID: nil
157	                )
158	                do {
159	                    guard let params = notification.params else {
160	                        continue
161	                    }
162	                    let decodeStartedAt = Date()
163	                    let update = try params.decoded(as: ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO.self)
164	                    PerformanceProbe.event(
165	                        "dock.stream.notification_decoded",
166	                        fields: [
167	                            "host_id": host.id,
168	                            "route": updateRoute,
169	                            "kind": update.kind.rawValue,
170	                            "seq": "\(update.seq)",
171	                            "generation": "\(update.generation)",
172	                            "rows": "\(update.rows?.count ?? 0)",
173	                            "projection_ids": "\(update.projectionIDs?.count ?? 0)",
174	                            "complete": update.complete.map(String.init) ?? "none",
175	                            "total_rows": update.totalRows.map(String.init) ?? "none",
176	                            "duration_ms": "\(PerformanceProbe.milliseconds(since: decodeStartedAt))",
177	                        ]
178	                    )
179	                    updateContinuation.yield(update)
180	                } catch {
181	                    updateContinuation.finish(throwing: AppServerClientError.responseDecoding(error.localizedDescription))
182	                    return
183	                }
184	            }
185	            updateContinuation.finish()
186	        }
187	    }
188	
189	    deinit {
190	        notificationTask?.cancel()
191	        updateContinuation.finish()
192	    }
193	
194	    public func subscribe() async throws -> ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO {
195	        let route = Self.subscribeRoute(for: view)
196	        DockLog.dock.notice("thread card stream subscribe started view=\(self.view.rawValue, privacy: .public) host_id=\(self.host.id, privacy: .public)")
197	        let context = AppServerRequestObservabilityContext(
198	            configuredHostID: host.id,
199	            route: route,
200	            store: observabilityStore
201	        )
202	        let response = try await client.sendRequest(
203	            method: route,
204	            timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.defaultRequestTimeout,
205	            observabilityContext: context,
206	            as: ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO.self
207	        )
208	        PerformanceProbe.event(
209	            "dock.stream.subscribe_response",
210	            fields: [
211	                "host_id": host.id,
212	                "route": route,
213	                "kind": response.kind.rawValue,
214	                "seq": "\(response.seq)",
215	                "generation": "\(response.generation)",
216	                "rows": "\(response.rows?.count ?? 0)",
217	                "projection_ids": "\(response.projectionIDs?.count ?? 0)",
218	                "complete": response.complete.map(String.init) ?? "none",
219	                "total_rows": response.totalRows.map(String.init) ?? "none",
220	            ]
221	        )
222	        DockLog.dock.notice("thread card stream subscribe finished view=\(self.view.rawValue, privacy: .public) host_id=\(self.host.id, privacy: .public) seq=\(response.seq, privacy: .public)")
223	        return response
224	    }
225	
226	    public func resync() async throws -> ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO {
227	        let route = Self.resyncRoute(for: view)
228	        let context = AppServerRequestObservabilityContext(
229	            configuredHostID: host.id,
230	            route: route,
231	            store: observabilityStore
232	        )
233	        let response = try await client.sendRequest(
234	            method: route,
235	            timeout: CodexDockConstants.AppServer.defaultRequestTimeout,
236	            observabilityContext: context,
237	            as: ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO.self
238	        )
239	        PerformanceProbe.event(
240	            "dock.stream.resync_response",
241	            fields: [
242	                "host_id": host.id,
243	                "route": route,
244	                "kind": response.kind.rawValue,
245	                "seq": "\(response.seq)",
246	                "generation": "\(response.generation)",
247	                "rows": "\(response.rows?.count ?? 0)",
248	                "projection_ids": "\(response.projectionIDs?.count ?? 0)",
249	                "complete": response.complete.map(String.init) ?? "none",
250	                "total_rows": response.totalRows.map(String.init) ?? "none",
251	            ]
252	        )
253	        return response
254	    }
255	
256	    public nonisolated func updates() -> AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error> {
257	        updateStream
258	    }
259	
260	    public func close() async {
261	        notificationTask?.cancel()
262	        updateContinuation.finish()
263	        await client.disconnect()
264	    }
265	
266	    private static func subscribeRoute(for view: ThreadCardStreamView) -> String {
267	        switch view {
268	        case .dock:
269	            return AppServerMethods.dockSubscribe
270	        case .archive:
271	            return AppServerMethods.archiveSubscribe
272	        }
273	    }
274	
275	    private static func updateRoute(for view: ThreadCardStreamView) -> String {
276	        switch view {
277	        case .dock:
278	            return AppServerMethods.dockUpdate
279	        case .archive:
280	            return AppServerMethods.archiveUpdate
281	        }
282	    }
283	
284	    private static func resyncRoute(for view: ThreadCardStreamView) -> String {
285	        switch view {
286	        case .dock:
287	            return AppServerMethods.dockResync
288	        case .archive:
289	            return AppServerMethods.archiveResync
290	        }
291	    }
292	}

2	import Foundation
3	
4	enum DockScreenState: Equatable, Sendable {
5	    case configurationError(String)
6	    case idle([DockHostViewModel])
7	    case loading([DockHostViewModel])
8	    case loaded(DockRenderSnapshot)
9	}
10	
11	@MainActor
12	final class DockScreenStore: ObservableObject {
13	    @Published private(set) var state: DockScreenState
14	    @Published private(set) var options: DockProjectionOptions
15	    @Published private(set) var searchText: String
16	    @Published private(set) var actionError: String?
17	
18	    private let coalescer: RenderCoalescer<DockRenderSnapshot>
19	    private let now: @Sendable () -> Date
20	    private var renderTask: Task<Void, Never>?
21	    private var searchDebounceTask: Task<Void, Never>?
22	    private var latestRevision = RenderRevision.zero
23	
24	    init(
25	        hosts: [DockHostViewModel],
26	        options: DockProjectionOptions = DockProjectionOptions(),
27	        coalescer: RenderCoalescer<DockRenderSnapshot> = RenderCoalescer<DockRenderSnapshot>(),
28	        now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = Date.init
29	    ) {
30	        self.state = .idle(hosts)
31	        self.options = options
32	        self.searchText = options.searchText
33	        self.coalescer = coalescer
34	        self.now = now
35	        self.actionError = nil
36	    }
37	
38	    init(configurationError message: String) {
39	        self.state = .configurationError(message)
40	        self.options = DockProjectionOptions()
41	        self.searchText = ""
42	        self.coalescer = RenderCoalescer<DockRenderSnapshot>()
43	        self.now = Date.init
44	        self.actionError = nil
45	    }
46	
47	    deinit {
48	        renderTask?.cancel()
49	        searchDebounceTask?.cancel()
50	    }
51	
52	    func start() {
53	        guard renderTask == nil else {
54	            return
55	        }
56	
57	        renderTask = Task { [weak self, coalescer] in

3	struct DockRenderProjector: Sendable {
4	    let now: @Sendable () -> Date
5	
6	    init(now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = Date.init) {
7	        self.now = now
8	    }
9	
10	    func snapshot(
11	        from input: DockRenderInput,
12	        localMetadata: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
13	    ) -> DockSnapshot {
14	        let startedAt = Date()
15	        let rowProjector = ThreadCardRowProjector(
16	            hosts: input.hosts,
17	            hostIdentityResolver: input.hostIdentityResolver,
18	            localMetadata: localMetadata,
19	            now: now
20	        )
21	        let liveRows = input.hosts.flatMap { host in
22	            rowProjector.rows(
23	                from: input.cardsByHostID[host.id] ?? [],
24	                configuredHostID: host.id
25	            )
26	        }
27	        // Local metadata may decorate relay rows, but it must never create card
28	        // rows. The relay is the single source of truth for card existence and order.
29	
30	        let snapshot = DockSnapshot(
31	            host: DockHostViewModel(host: input.hosts[0]),
32	            hosts: input.hosts.map(DockHostViewModel.init),
33	            hostStates: input.hostStates,
34	            hostIdentityResolver: input.hostIdentityResolver,
35	            rows: liveRows,
36	            isPartial: input.isPartial
37	        )
38	        if PerformanceProbe.isEnabled {
39	            let hostCardCounts = input.hosts
40	                .map { "\($0.id):\(input.cardsByHostID[$0.id]?.count ?? 0)" }
41	                .joined(separator: ",")
42	            PerformanceProbe.event(
43	                "dock.snapshot.project",
44	                fields: [
45	                    "hosts": "\(input.hosts.count)",
46	                    "host_cards": hostCardCounts,
47	                    "rows": "\(snapshot.rows.count)",
48	                    "metadata_entries": "\(localMetadata.count)",
49	                    "partial": "\(snapshot.isPartial)",
50	                    "duration_ms": "\(PerformanceProbe.milliseconds(since: startedAt))",
51	                ]
52	            )
53	        }
54	        return snapshot
55	    }
56	
57	    func render(
58	        snapshot: DockSnapshot,
59	        options: DockProjectionOptions,
60	        revision: RenderRevision
61	    ) -> DockRenderSnapshot {
62	        let startedAt = Date()
63	        let renderSnapshot = DockRenderSnapshot(
64	            revision: revision,
65	            snapshot: snapshot,
66	            projection: snapshot.project(options: options)
67	        )
68	        if PerformanceProbe.isEnabled {
69	            PerformanceProbe.event(
70	                "dock.render.project",
71	                fields: [
72	                    "revision": "\(revision.rawValue)",

77	                    "filters": "\(options.filters.activeFilterCount)",
78	                    "duration_ms": "\(PerformanceProbe.milliseconds(since: startedAt))",
79	                ]

3	public actor RenderCoalescer<Snapshot: Sendable> {
4	    public let snapshots: AsyncStream<Snapshot>
5	
6	    private let continuation: AsyncStream<Snapshot>.Continuation
7	    private var latestAcceptedRevision: RenderRevision?
8	
9	    public init(
10	        bufferingNewest: Int = CodexDockConstants.Rendering.renderStreamBufferNewest
11	    ) {
12	        let stream = AsyncStream.makeStream(
13	            of: Snapshot.self,
14	            bufferingPolicy: .bufferingNewest(bufferingNewest)
15	        )
16	        self.snapshots = stream.stream
17	        self.continuation = stream.continuation
18	    }
19	
20	    public func submit(_ snapshot: Snapshot, revision: RenderRevision) {
21	        if let latestAcceptedRevision,
22	           revision < latestAcceptedRevision {
23	            PerformanceProbe.event(
24	                "render.coalescer.drop_stale",
25	                fields: [
26	                    "revision": "\(revision.rawValue)",
27	                    "latest_revision": "\(latestAcceptedRevision.rawValue)",
28	                ]
29	            )
30	            return
31	        }
32	
33	        latestAcceptedRevision = revision
34	        let result = continuation.yield(snapshot)
35	        PerformanceProbe.event(
36	            "render.coalescer.submit",
37	            fields: [
38	                "revision": "\(revision.rawValue)",
39	                "yield_result": "\(result)",
40	            ]
41	        )
42	    }
43	
44	    public func stream() -> AsyncStream<Snapshot> {
45	        snapshots
46	    }
47	
48	    public func latestRevision() -> RenderRevision? {
49	        latestAcceptedRevision
50	    }
51	
52	    public func finish() {
53	        continuation.finish()
54	    }
55	}

43	public struct ResolvedDockHost: Equatable, Sendable {
44	    public let logicalHostID: String
45	    public let host: DockHostConfiguration
46	    public let configuredHostIDs: [String]
47	    public let displayName: String
48	    public let endpoint: String
49	}
